entities.title: A public repository needs nothing
entities.statement: A public GitHub or GitLab repository opens from its address alone, with no sign-in, token or setup.
entities.rationale: The browser is how people are pointed at a repository; any step before it loses them.
acceptanceCriteria: A link with ?url= opens the repository's first folder.

entities.title: A token goes to its host alone
entities.summary: A reader's token never leaves their browser except to the host it is for.
entities.statement: A token is kept only in the reader's browser, under the host it was saved for, and sent only in requests to that host.
entities.rationale: Readers must be able to read private repositories without trusting anyone else with their access; a GitHub token must never reach a self-hosted GitLab.
acceptanceCriteria: Requests to other hosts carry no token.
Nothing about the token is sent to the site that serves the page.

entities.title: Every kind is shown
entities.summary: Every view and knowledge kind the skills and catalogue define is shown.
entities.statement: The browser shows the four diagrams, the five behavior views and all twenty-five knowledge kinds; a file of a kind it doesn't know is skipped and named.
entities.rationale: A file the browser can't show is a file nobody reads.
acceptanceCriteria: Each kind in Meta/Agents/Skills and Meta/Agents/Knowledge has a place in the page.
An unknown kind appears in the status line.

entities.title: Nothing recorded is hidden
entities.summary: Every field of every record is shown, named or not.
entities.statement: Every field a knowledge record carries is shown, including fields no schema names; every diagram is also available as tables.
entities.rationale: The catalogue allows any field so that agents don't lose what they know; the reader must see it.
acceptanceCriteria: A record with an extra field shows it, labelled from its name.
Each drawn view has its full tables under it.

entities.title: Everything has an address
entities.summary: Each folder, part, view and record can be linked to.
entities.statement: The address names the repository, and after # the folder and the part, view or record being shown, so a copied address opens the same place.
entities.rationale: Pointing someone at one thing is how reviews and questions start.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening a copied address shows the same folder and selects the same part or record.

entities.title: Works without the drawing library
entities.summary: If dagre fails to load, everything is still readable.
entities.statement: When the layout library cannot load or a drawing fails, the view is shown as its tables, and the status line says so.
entities.rationale: The tables are the whole of each view; the drawing is a way into them.
acceptanceCriteria: With dagre blocked, every view's tables open.

entities.title: Works without WebGL
entities.summary: Without WebGL or three.js, everything is still readable in Flat.
entities.statement: When the browser has no WebGL 2, or three.js can't load, a Cyberspace address shows the same place in Flat and the status line says why; without WebGL the mode switch is not offered. When the 3D view's context is lost, the status line says so and offers to restore it.
entities.rationale: Cyberspace is another way into the same data, never the only one (decisions tables-always and cyberspace-mode).
acceptanceCriteria: With WebGL turned off, #|~space shows the root folder flat and says: Cyberspace needs WebGL, which this browser has turned off. Showing the flat view.
With jsDelivr's three.js blocked, #|~space shows the root folder flat and says: Cyberspace couldn't load its 3D library. Showing the flat view.
When the WebGL context is lost, the status line says The 3D view stopped, and Restore it builds the view again.

entities.title: One static file
entities.summary: No build, and no server needed.
entities.statement: The page is one HTML file that runs in the reader's browser, with its libraries from a CDN, and works served as a static file; sign-in with GitHub is the only thing that needs its Worker.
entities.rationale: Anyone can host it, copy it or run it from disk, and a reader who doesn't sign in gives no server their repository or token.
acceptanceCriteria: index.html served by any static server works, with pasted tokens in place of sign-in.

entities.title: Says what is waiting
entities.summary: Open decisions and blockers across the repository are gathered in one place.
entities.statement: Every open decision and unresolved blocker in the repository is listed in one view, with who it waits on and what it blocks.
entities.rationale: In this way of working, what waits on a person is what agents most need them to see.
acceptanceCriteria: A decision with status open appears in Waiting; one with another status does not.
